Provider Credentialing & Enrollment

One Wrong Date Can Mean Months of Delay

Credentialing is more than filling out forms. Each application has to match licensing data exactly, and payer rules shift constantly. Without careful management, privileges stall, reimbursements slow down, and in-network access can quietly slip away while a provider waits.

PMEX handles the full process of a provider's insurance enrollment from start to finish: gathering and verifying licenses, certifications and training records, completing payer applications, tracking their progress, and following up with insurance panels until approval is in hand. The same team maintains ongoing recredentialing so compliance never lapses.

Every file is worked to payer standards to shorten approval timelines and keep credentialing in sync with your practice's actual goals, so you stay in network, on schedule, and ahead of expiration dates.

Our Credentialing Process

From First Survey to Ongoing Monitoring

The typical industry timeline is 60 to 120 days. PMEX's enrollment officers engage payers weekly to work every file as fast as it can move.

1

Surveying the Provider

An in-depth interview gathers license numbers, educational history, demographics and professional background.

2

Choosing the Insurance Company

Insurance partners are chosen strategically, aligned to your practice goals, license type and location.

3

Enrollment & Management

CAQH application submission, profile management and payer enrollment for smooth primary source verification.

4

Fast Approvals

Weekly engagement with payers advocates for rapid processing and endorsement of the application.

5

In-Network Enrollment

The contract phase covers fee schedules and eligible CPT codes, with closed-panel appeals handled if needed.

6

Winning Hospital Privileges

Support in gaining admitting, courtesy or surgical privileges once credentialing wraps up.

7

Ongoing Monitoring

Credentialing expirations are tracked with daily and weekly reviews, keeping active status intact without interruption.

Nationwide Coverage

One Credentialing Team, Licensed to Navigate All 50 States

Every state runs its own medical board, its own Medicaid program, and often its own timelines and paperwork quirks on top of whatever a payer requires nationally. A credentialing file that sails through Texas can stall for a completely different reason in New York. PMEX tracks all of it under one team, so a multi-state group practice doesn't need a different vendor, or a different point of contact, for every state it operates in.
